title: control-plane: add RBAC v2 core types + authz middleware hook
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
description:
Summary
This PR introduces the foundational RBAC v2 primitives (Resource / Action / Scope) and wires a single authorization middleware hook into the control-plane service request path.

This is intentionally “plumbing + types” only. It does not attempt to inventory or guard every endpoint yet. The immediate goal is to establish a consistent, testable place to perform checks so follow-on PRs can add permissions endpoint-by-endpoint without re-implementing evaluation / error handling.

Context
We’re moving from RBAC v1 feature-gated checks (inconsistent and often implicit) to an explicit permission model that supports enterprise requirements: separation of duties, least privilege, and explainable auditability. See ENG-5381 (project) and ENG-5383 (taxonomy).

What’s in this PR
- Core RBAC v2 types:
  - Resource: typed identifier for “what” we’re protecting (e.g. org, project, api_key, model_deployment).
  - Action: verb-like capability (e.g. read, list, create, update, delete, rotate, export).
  - Scope: “where” the permission applies (org-wide vs project-scoped), including a consistent serialization format for logs/metrics.
- A central authz middleware hook:
  - Adds an AuthzContext to request context (actor id/type, org id, project id, request id, ip, user-agent).
  - Provides a single entry point to call an evaluator (interface) that will be implemented/extended in follow-ups.
  - Implements structured allow/deny logging fields (without changing audit-log exporter yet; that’s in a later PR).
- A minimal “Noop/AllowAll” evaluator for integration wiring in staging.
- A deny response shape that the console and API clients can reliably handle (HTTP 403 + machine-readable reason code), but with conservative defaults to avoid breaking current flows while under a feature flag.

Design notes
- Evaluation is invoked only when a handler declares a PermissionRequirement (resource/action/scope). If no requirement is declared, behavior is unchanged for now.
- The middleware is placed after authentication and org/project resolution so we can include concrete scope identifiers.
- This PR defines the canonical string forms used for metrics/logging:
  - resource: "org", "project", "api_key", ...
  - action: "read", "create", "rotate", ...
  - scope: "org:{org_id}" or "project:{project_id}" (plus future forms like "dedicated_cluster:{id}")

Changed areas (high level)
- control-plane/authz/:
  - rbac_types.go: Resource, Action, Scope types + parsing/validation helpers
  - evaluator.go: Evaluator interface + Decision struct
  - middleware.go: AuthzMiddleware + context wiring
- control-plane/http/:
  - router wiring to install middleware once
  - small refactor: ensure org/project resolution happens before authz hook
- control-plane/handlers/:
  - adds optional permission declaration pattern (no endpoints enforced yet)
- tests:
  - unit tests for scope parsing/serialization
  - middleware tests for context propagation + 403 shape

Illustrative snippets (trimmed)
- Permission requirement declaration (pattern only; not widely used yet):
  - RequirePermission(ResourceProject, ActionUpdate, ScopeProject(projectID))
- Middleware behavior:
  - if feature flag off -> skip evaluation, continue
  - if requirement missing -> continue
  - if evaluator returns deny -> 403 with {"error":"forbidden","reason":"RBAC_DENY","resource":"...","action":"...","scope":"..."}

Commits (squash summary)
1) authz: define RBAC v2 core types and canonical string forms
2) control-plane: add AuthzMiddleware and context plumbing
3) tests: scope parse/roundtrip + middleware deny response
4) refactor: ensure org/project resolution precedes authz hook

Rollout / safety
- Middleware is behind feature flag: control_plane.rbac_v2_middleware_enabled (default false).
- With flag enabled, we still only evaluate when an endpoint opts in by declaring a requirement. This prevents surprise behavior changes while we inventory endpoints.
- Follow-ups will introduce shadow evaluation and metrics (ENG-5389 / later PR) before enforcement.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Wire real policy evaluation + caching (ENG-5384)
- Add standardized reason codes and client messaging (separate PR; see ENG-5384)
- Endpoint-by-endpoint permission annotations + enforcement (ENG-5385)
- Audit log enrichment with authz decision context (ENG-5387)

Review conversation (highlights)
- Jordan Lee (policy engine): “Can we make Scope serialization stable and unambiguous? We’ll need it for policy evaluation inputs and audit logs.”
  - Kaitlyn Nguyen: Updated Scope to use explicit prefixes (org:/project:) and added parse/roundtrip tests.
- Marcus Lin (security): “We should avoid ‘silent allow’ when requirement is present but evaluator is misconfigured. At minimum log it.”
  - Kaitlyn Nguyen: Added WARN log when evaluator is nil and requirement exists; returns deny only when flag enabled + evaluator present. Also added a metric stub (authz_eval_skipped_total) to fill in later.
- Ethan Park (control plane lead): “Placement looks good, but make sure auth middleware runs after authn and tenant resolution. We’ve been burned by missing org_id in logs.”
  - Kaitlyn Nguyen: Refactored router order; added middleware test to assert org_id in authz context.
- Allison Grant (logging standards): “Please standardize log field names now to avoid schema churn later.”
  - Kaitlyn Nguyen: Normalized fields to authz.resource/authz.action/authz.scope/authz.decision and ensured request_id present.

CI / checks
- build: pass
- unit tests: pass
- lint: pass
- integration (control-plane): pass

Notes for release
No customer-visible changes with defaults. This is a prerequisite for RBAC v2 enforcement work and will be enabled only in staging while we begin endpoint inventory + policy evaluation integration.
release_notes: Internal-only plumbing for RBAC v2: introduces Resource/Action/Scope primitives and a central authz middleware hook (feature-flagged). No behavior change by default.
